organisation.name: AGE Platform Europe
organisation.category: Non-governmental organisations, platforms and networks and similar
organisation.goals:
AGE Platform Europe is a European network of non-profit organisations of and for older people, which aims to voice and promote older persons' rights and interest and to elevate their voice at EU and international level.
AGE’s vision encompasses an inclusive society, based on well-being for all, solidarity between generations and full entitlement to enjoy life, participate in and contribute to society. At the same time, each person’s rights and responsibilities throughout their life course have to be fully respected.
AGE celebrates longevity as one of the greatest achievements of humanity. We seek to combat ageism, promote human rights throughout the life course, reduce inequalities and enable everyone to live a full and dignified life.
To achieve this mission:
- We raise the aspirations and needs of older people bridging the gap between them and policymakers
- We transform our members’ experiences and ideas into policy proposals, advocacy,
- We support our members’ active involvement

consultation.title: Strategy on Victims' Rights - Public Consultation
consultation.summary: The European Commission has launched a public consultation for the EU Strategy on victims’ rights covering the period from 2026 to 2030. This initiative aims to consolidate the EU framework for protecting victims of crime and ensures that these rights are effectively exercised across all Member States. It builds upon the achievements of the previous 2020 to 2025 strategy while addressing newly emerging threats. Furthermore, the strategy will complement the provisionally agreed revision of the Victims’ rights Directive with non-legislative measures.
key_points: Consolidates the EU framework for protecting victims of crime
Focuses on the effective practical exercise of victims' rights across Member States
Builds on the achievements of the 2020 to 2025 victims' rights strategy
Addresses new emerging threats
Complements the provisionally agreed revision of the Victims’ rights Directive with non-legislative measures

organisation.name: Acumen Public Affairs
organisation.goals: Acumen Public Affairs is an independent consultancy set up in 2010 to combine the very best of big agency experience with hands-on senior support. Our founding partners have an unrivalled track record in public affairs and strategic communications working for corporations, governments, trade associations, NGOs and international institutions in Brussels, Geneva and beyond.

consultation.short_title: Revision of EU rules on public procurement
consultation.title: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL on public contracts and concessions, repealing Directives 2014/23/EU, 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU, and amending Regulations (EC) No 1370/2007, (EU) 2023/1542, (EU) 2024/1157, (EU) 2024/1252, (EU) 2024/1735, (EU) 2024/1781, (EU) 2024/2847, (EU) 2024/3110 and (EU) 2025/40, and Directives 2008/98/EC, (EU) 2019/882, (EU) 2022/2381, (EU) 2023/1791 and (EU) 2024/1760 (Public Procurement Act)
consultation.summary: The European Commission proposes a revision of EU public procurement rules through a new regulation that repeals the existing 2014 directives on public procurement, utilities, and concessions. The initiative aims to modernize and simplify rules, reduce administrative burdens, and enable preferences for European products in strategic sectors to secure supply chains and add EU value. It also amends multiple sector-specific regulations and directives containing procurement provisions to improve coherence and transparency. Furthermore, the proposal addresses high administrative burdens and legal uncertainty identified in previous evaluations regarding public buyers and businesses.
key_points: Revises and replaces Directives 2014/23/EU, 2014/24/EU, and 2014/25/EU with a single Public Procurement Act regulation.
Enables preference for European products in strategic sectors to ensure security of supply and EU added value.
Aims to modernize and simplify rules, specifically considering EU start-ups and innovators.
Amends various sector-specific regulations and directives that contain public procurement provisions.
Addresses administrative burdens and legal uncertainty that currently affect public buyers and businesses, including SMEs.

consultation.short_title: Omnibus simplification of energy-efficient product legislation
consultation.title: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL amending Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 and Regulation (EU) 2020/740 as regards simplification and better use of digital options for energy and tyre labelling
consultation.summary: The European Commission proposes an omnibus regulation to simplify and improve the use of digital options under Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 for energy labelling and Regulation (EU) 2020/740 for tyre labelling. The initiative aims to reduce administrative burdens and lower compliance costs for businesses while maintaining consumer protection and product transparency. It introduces targeted amendments to make label delivery, display rules, and database registration more effective. The proposal builds on previous implementation reports, stakeholder consultations, and an impact assessment.
key_points: Amends Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 on energy labelling and Regulation (EU) 2020/740 on tyre labelling.
Aims to reduce administrative costs and burdens for businesses.
Simplifies rules for complying with energy and tyre label delivery and display.
Facilitates simpler registration in the European Product Registry for Energy Labelling (EPREL).
Improves surveillance and compliance within the regulatory framework.
Allows for the possibility of amending the tyre label via delegated acts.

organisation.name: CEFIC - European Chemical Industry Council
organisation.goals: Cefic is a not-for-profit making organisation devoted to promote a thriving European Chemical Industry that is broadly recognised to provide sustainable, safe, innovative and resource efficient solutions to foster prosperity, growth and investments in Europe and meet the challenges for future generations. Our main purpose is to serve the Members and the European chemical industry by generating and aggregating scientific knowledge, to contribute to the development of the industry by providing support to all its Members. In view of supporting this main purpose, Cefic may (i) engage, represent and advocate in a focussed and effective manner the interests of its Members and the industry at a European level by creating the appropriate support and policy frameworks for said industry in Europe and beyond as well as (ii) develop, promote and defend common industry positions.

consultation.title: Commission Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing diversification instrument to address critical strategic dependencies that expose the Union to economic security risks
consultation.summary: The European Commission is preparing a diversification package, including a new trade instrument and supporting measures, to address critical strategic dependencies on single supplier countries. The initiative aims to accelerate supply chain resilience and reduce economic security risks in critical sectors where non-EU countries may use dependencies as leverage. It combines trade policy measures based on Article 207 TFEU with single market measures based on Article 114 TFEU to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework. This call for evidence invites public and stakeholder feedback to inform the Commission's impact assessment and future legislative work.
key_points: Targets concentrated critical dependencies on dominant supplier countries for strategic sectors.
Proposes a new trade diversification instrument complemented by regulatory and financial support measures.
Combines trade policy measures under Article 207 TFEU and Single Market measures under Article 114 TFEU.
Seeks to address market gaps such as the lack of appropriate price signals and incentives for business de-risking.
Aims to protect the EU from supply chain disruptions, geopolitical pressure, and market volatility.

organisation.name: Centre for European Policy Studies
organisation.goals:
CEPS is among the most authoritative think tanks operating in the European Union. CEPS serves as a leading forum for debate on EU affairs, but its most distinguishing feature lies in its strong in-house research capacity, complemented by an extensive network of partners. CEPS is an independent, not-for-profit institution that provides high-quality research without promoting the interests of any other organisation or company. Goals:
- To carry out state-of-the-art policy research leading to solutions to European challenges
- To provide a forum for discussion among all stakeholders in the European policy process
- To build collaborative networks of researchers, policy-makers, NGO and business representatives across Europe
- To disseminate our findings and views through a regular flow of publications and public events

organisation.name: Climate Action Network Europe
organisation.category: Non-governmental organisations, platforms and networks and similar
organisation.goals:
Climate Action Network (CAN) Europe is recognised as Europe's leading network working on climate and energy issues. With over 200 member organisations active in 40 European countries, representing over 1700 NGOs and more than 40 million citizens, CAN Europe unites to work to prevent dangerous climate change and promote sustainable energy and environment policy in Europe.
The Climate Action Network (CAN) International is a worldwide network of over 1500 Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) working to promote government, private sector and individual action to limit human-induced climate change to ecologically sustainable levels. CAN is based on trust, openness and democracy.
The vision of CAN is a world striving actively towards and achieving the protection of the global climate in a manner that promotes equity and social justice between peoples, sustainable development of all communities, and protection of the global environment. CAN unites to work towards this vision.

consultation.short_title: Minimum performance standards for data centres in Europe
consultation.title: Establishment of common Union minimum performance standards for data centres located in its territory
consultation.summary: The European Commission is preparing an initiative to establish common Union minimum performance standards for data centres located in its territory. Building on existing reporting and rating schemes under the Energy Efficiency Directive, the proposed regulation aims to phase out unsustainable practices and technologies in new or retrofitted facilities. The initiative seeks to address rising energy and water consumption, limited waste heat reuse, and regulatory fragmentation across Member States. An impact assessment is planned for late 2026, with a legislative proposal anticipated in the second quarter of 2027.
key_points: Establish common EU minimum performance standards for data centres regarding energy efficiency, water use, waste-heat reuse, and grid services.
Form the third step in the EU sustainability framework for data centres, following the 2024 reporting scheme and the 2026 rating scheme.
Prevent divergent national approaches and reduce regulatory fragmentation across Member States.
Improve sector competitiveness and reduce operational costs by cutting energy and water waste.
Support energy system integration by aligning data centre operations with power grid and heat network needs.
Prepare an impact assessment in Q4 2026 to support the drafting of the legislative proposal for Q2 2027.

consultation.short_title: Common format for initial and updated National Air Pollution Control Programmes
consultation.title: COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION (EU) …/… laying down rules for the application of Directive (EU) 2016/2284 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the common format for national air pollution control programmes and repealing Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/1522
consultation.summary: This Commission implementing decision lays down a revised common format for national air pollution control programmes under Directive (EU) 2016/2284. It aims to simplify and clarify reporting requirements, improve data comparability, and support Member States in planning measures to meet national emission reduction commitments. The decision repeals the previous Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/1522 and introduces a 12-month transitional period allowing Member States to use either the old or the new format. The annex details specific reporting sections covering general information, policy frameworks, emission inventories, air quality status, and projected impacts.
key_points: Establishes a revised common format for initial and updated National Air Pollution Control Programmes (NAPCPs).
Repeals Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/1522.
Grants a 12-month transitional period where Member States can use either the previous or the new format.

Requires structured reporting on general administrative information, air quality policy frameworks, current emission and air quality situations, transboundary impacts, and adopted policies and measures.
Mandates quantitative projections of future emissions for key pollutants including SO2, NOx, NMVOC, NH3, and PM2.5.

organisation.name: Confédération des Syndicats Chrétiens de Belgique
organisation.goals: La Confédération des Syndicats Chrétiens (CSC) est la première organisation syndicale de Belgique avec 1.482.810 affilié.e.s (état: 02/04/2024).

consultation.short_title: Tackling unjustified territorial supply constraints in the Single Market
consultation.title: Public consultation on Territorial Supply Constraints
consultation.summary: The European Commission has launched a public consultation on territorial supply constraints, which are limitations imposed by large manufacturers to prevent retailers from buying products in one Member State and reselling them in another. These practices fragment the Single Market, limit consumer choice, and lead to significant price differences for daily consumer goods across the EU. The initiative aims to introduce new tools to address these constraints beyond situations currently captured by competition law, as announced in the May 2025 Single Market Strategy. This consultation gathers input from stakeholders to better understand the impact and scale of these supply restrictions.
key_points: Territorial supply constraints hinder retailers from buying goods in one Member State to resell in another
Such practices fragment the Single Market and limit consumer choice
They contribute to significant price differences for daily consumer goods across the EU
The initiative follows the Single Market Strategy announced in May 2025
New tools are proposed to address these constraints beyond existing competition law

organisation.name: Corporate Europe Observatory
organisation.category: Non-governmental organisations, platforms and networks and similar
organisation.goals: Corporate Europe Observatory (CEO) is a research and campaign group working to expose and challenge the privileged access and influence enjoyed by corporations and their lobby groups in EU policy making. Corporate Europe Observatory is strongly committed to transparency about EU lobbying. CEO believes that the Transparency Register fails basic transparency standards and does not yet live up to its name. We support a legally-binding register, stronger safeguards against inaccurate reporting, and the publication of the names of all individual interest representatives. We regret that the 2021 register revamp no longer requires NGOs and think tanks to submit a figure for an annual lobby spend. We will continue to provide such a figure in the notes below. We also regret that the names of individual lobbyists can no longer be provided.

organisation.name: DIGITALEUROPE
organisation.goals: DIGITALEUROPE represents the digitally transforming industries in Europe. DIGITALEUROPE wants a European Union that nurtures and supports digital technology industries, and that prospers from the jobs we provide, the innovation and economic benefits we deliver and the societal challenges we address. Our mission is to foster, on behalf of our members, a business, policy and regulatory environment in Europe that best realises our vision. We will achieve this by working as positive partners with the European Institutions and other European and global bodies and, through our national trade associations, the member states of Europe. DIGITALEUROPE’s members include 122 Corporate members and 42 National Trade Associations from across Europe.

consultation.title: Public Consultation on the Evaluation of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (Dual-Use Regulation)
consultation.summary: The European Commission has launched a public consultation to evaluate Regulation (EU) 2021/821 on the control of exports, brokering, technical assistance, transit, and transfer of dual-use items. Pursuant to Article 26(4) of the Regulation, the evaluation aims to determine whether the rules have achieved their objectives and remain effective. It also assesses the legislation in light of the evolving global geopolitical landscape and new security threats. Furthermore, the evaluation examines potential ways to reduce administrative burdens for businesses.
key_points: Evaluation of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 on dual-use items
Assessment of whether the Regulation has achieved its objectives
Review of relevance in view of the evolving global geopolitical landscape
Analysis of new threats requiring regulatory adjustments
Identification of ways to reduce administrative burden for businesses

consultation.short_title: European partnerships implemented as joint undertakings under Horizon Europe (2028-2034)
consultation.title: Single Basic Act for Joint Undertakings and thematic priorities for the European Partnership portfolio in Horizon Europe 28-34
consultation.summary: The European Commission is consulting on the role of European partnerships implemented as joint undertakings under the Horizon Europe framework programme for 2028-2034. The initiative proposes simplifying the instrument by streamlining implementation modes and applying a portfolio approach to identify a limited set of coherent partnerships. These partnerships will feature objectives closely aligned with the Competitiveness Fund. Furthermore, the proposal suggests establishing joint undertakings under Article 187 TFEU through a single basic act with harmonised rules.
key_points: Streamline implementation modes for European partnerships under Horizon Europe 2028-2034
Use a portfolio approach to identify a limited set of coherent partnerships
Align partnership objectives closely with the Competitiveness Fund
Establish joint undertakings under Article 187 TFEU with clear added value
Implement a single basic act with harmonised rules for joint undertakings

organisation.name: Egmont - Royal Institute for International Relations
organisation.goals:
The Royal Institute for International Relations is an independent think-tank based in Brussels. Its interdisciplinary research is conducted in a spirit of total academic freedom. Drawing on the expertise of its own research fellows, as well as that of external specialists, both Belgian and foreign, it provides analysis and policy options that are meant to be as operational as possible.
Along with research and meetings, the Institute has also developed specialised training activities, both in Brussels and abroad. It can, on request, offer specific programmes for visiting and resident diplomats and foreign professionals. Close cooperation with other research centres, both in Belgium, in Europe and beyond, has resulted in a growing number of joint conferences and in more structured cooperations on research and publications. This has proved to be mutually beneficial and enriching.

consultation.short_title: Review of the International Procurement Instrument
consultation.title: Report from the Commission to the European Parliament and to the Council on the review of the scope, functioning and efficiency of Regulation (EU) 2022/1031 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 June 2022 on the access of third-country economic operators, goods and services to the Union’s public procurement and concession markets and procedures supporting negotiations on access of Union economic operators, goods and services to the public procurement and concession markets of third countries (International Procurement Instrument - IPI)
consultation.summary: The European Commission is conducting a review of the scope, functioning, and efficiency of Regulation (EU) 2022/1031 on the International Procurement Instrument (IPI). The review evaluates the implementation of the regulation, including investigation processes, consultations, thresholds, exceptions, and the first adopted IPI measure regarding medical devices from China. It aims to assess the instrument's effectiveness in tackling procurement barriers in non-EU countries and ensuring a level playing field for EU operators. The findings will be presented in a report to the European Parliament and the Council by August 2027.
key_points: Review of the scope, functioning, and efficiency of the IPI Regulation pursuant to Article 14.
Assessment of investigation procedures, third-country consultations, thresholds, and types of measures.
Evaluation of the application and implementation of the first IPI measure concerning Chinese medical devices.
Analysis of the efficiency of online complaint tools and rules for determining origin.
Execution of a 12-week online public consultation through the Have your say portal.
Publication of a factual summary of consultation results and an implementation report to the European Parliament and the Council.

organisation.category: Non-governmental organisations, platforms and networks and similar
organisation.goals:
EUROCITIES activities
EUROCITIES works along three complementary strands of activities:
Influencing
With 75% of Europe’s population living in cities, our fundamental purpose as a network is to shape European policy - both to ensure it is based on front line experience and to increase recognition and resources for cities in addressing Europe’s strategic priorities. To this end, EUROCITIES works with the European Commission, both at political and technical level, as well as with the European Parliament, the Committee of the Regions and EU Member States, to ensure that climate, recovery, inclusion and other issues of interest for the local level are effectively addressed.
Networking
Our policy forums are the foundation of EUROCITIES as a multi-dimensional network, each promoting a rich exchange of views and experience through which, either as politicians or technical officers, our members have an opportunity to share knowledge, compare approaches, test innovative (...)

consultation.title: Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council and the European Economic and Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions on the creation of a new Atlantic Maritime and Macro-regional Strategy
consultation.summary: The European Commission is preparing a new EU Atlantic Maritime and Macro-regional Strategy to be adopted by June 2027, following a request from the European Council. Building on the existing Atlantic Maritime Strategy and Action Plan, the initiative aims to provide a broader, integrated territorial framework to address shared challenges and opportunities across the Atlantic region. It seeks to improve policy coordination, foster innovative solutions, strengthen multi-level governance, and increase the political weight of Atlantic priorities. The strategy targets the four EU Atlantic Member States and will be established through a non-legislative Communication without an impact assessment.
key_points: Development of a new EU Atlantic Maritime and Macro-regional Strategy by June 2027.
Builds on and integrates the Atlantic Maritime Strategy and the Atlantic Action Plan.
Aims to improve policy coordination across EU, national, and regional levels and funding instruments.
Restricted in scope to the four EU Atlantic Member States: France, Ireland, Portugal, and Spain.
Will incorporate a monitoring framework integrated into the Commission's biennial reports on macro-regional strategies.
Takes the form of a non-legislative Communication from the Commission without requiring an impact assessment.

organisation.category: Non-governmental organisations, platforms and networks and similar

consultation.short_title: Revision of Schengen short-stay visa procedures (recast)
consultation.title: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a Union Code on Visas (recast)
consultation.summary: The European Commission proposes a legislative recast of the EU Visa Code to make Schengen short-stay visa rules more strategic, secure, and effective. The initiative aims to improve cooperation with third countries on return, readmission, and security, while providing a framework to respond to unforeseen events or hostile actions. It also seeks to facilitate legitimate travel, particularly for business travellers linked to trusted companies, and addresses technical aspects related to the digitalisation of visa procedures. Additionally, the proposal explores the feasibility of an additional charge on top of the Schengen visa fee to support the common visa policy.
key_points: Strengthens tools linking visa policy to third-country cooperation on return, readmission, and border management.
Establishes a mechanism to suspend or restrict visa applications from specific travellers in response to hostile actions or emergencies.
Introduces a common EU approach to identify trusted companies and facilitate travel for their business representatives.
Improves local consular adaptations and addresses technical inconsistencies related to the digitalisation of visas.
Explores the introduction of a harmonised additional charge levied at EU level on top of the Schengen visa fee.
Includes consequential amendments to the Visa Regulation and the European Border and Coast Guard Regulation.

organisation.name: European Environmental Bureau
organisation.category: Non-governmental organisations, platforms and networks and similar
organisation.goals:
Set up in 1974, the EEB is Europe’s largest and most inclusive network of environmental citizens’ groups - and the only one that works on such a broad range of issues.
It currently consists of over 190 member organisations in 41 countries, including a growing number of networks, and representing some 30 million individual members and supporters.
Our vision is of a better future where people and nature thrive together. The next generation deserves a healthy planet. We believe in a world where equal, just, peaceful and democratic societies can prosper. A world with rich biodiversity and a safe climate. A world where laws and policies promote health and wellbeing while respecting nature. We believe that Europe has a crucial role to play in building this future and aim to contribute to efforts related to creating a better environment in the European Union and beyond.

consultation.title: REPORT FROM THE COMMISSION TO THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT, THE COUNCIL, THE EUROPEAN ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COMMITTEE AND THE COMMITTEE OF THE REGIONS identifying Member States at risk of not meeting the 2030 targets for the reduction of packaging waste and food waste, the preparing for re-use and recycling target for municipal waste, the recycling target for packaging waste and the 2035 municipal waste landfilling reduction target
consultation.summary: The European Commission is preparing the 2027 early warning report to assess Member States progress towards 2030 targets for municipal waste recycling, packaging waste reduction and recycling, and food waste reduction, alongside the 2035 municipal waste landfilling reduction target. The report identifies countries at risk of missing these targets and provides tailored recommendations and best practices to improve their performance. This initiative fulfils a legal obligation under EU waste directives without introducing new policy objectives or requiring an impact assessment. It focuses on evaluating national policies and implementation measures that directly impact waste prevention, separate collection, sorting, and recycling.
key_points: Assess progress towards 2030 waste reduction and recycling targets and 2035 landfill reduction targets.
Identify Member States at risk of not meeting the established targets.
Provide general and country-specific recommendations alongside best practice sharing.
Fulfill legal reporting obligations under the Waste Framework Directive, Packaging and Packaging Waste Directive, and Landfill Directive.
Incorporate data and methodology developed by the European Environment Agency and its European Topic Centre.
Include dedicated country-specific annexes for Member States identified at risk.

organisation.name: European Policy Centre
organisation.goals:
The European Policy Centre (EPC) is an independent, not-for-profit think tank dedicated to fostering European integration through analysis and debate, supporting and challenging European decision-makers at all levels to make informed decisions based on evidence and analysis, and providing a platform for engaging partners, stakeholders and citizens in EU policy-making and in the debate about the future of Europe.
In line with its multi-constituency approach, members of the EPC comprise companies, professional and business federations, trade unions, diplomatic missions, regional and local bodies, as well as NGOs representing a broad range of civil society interests, foundations, international and religious organisations. The EPC has around 400 member organisations. Membership changes throughout the year and the latest information can be found on the EPC website which is regularly updated: https://www.epc.eu/en/members

consultation.short_title: Proposal for a new Regulation on the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol)
consultation.title: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL on the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol), amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1726 and Regulation (EU) 2024/982, and repealing Regulation (EU) 2016/794
consultation.summary: The European Commission has proposed a new regulation on the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol) to reinforce its operational role in combating serious cross-border crime and terrorism. The initiative replaces Regulation (EU) 2016/794, updates Europol's mandate to address a changing security landscape, and provides for increased resources and staff. It also establishes structured cooperation between Europol and eu-LISA for information management and ICT services while ensuring full alignment with EU data protection frameworks.
key_points: Replaces Regulation (EU) 2016/794 to establish a revised mandate for Europol.
Aims to enhance Europol's operational capabilities against online and offline serious crime and terrorism.
Establishes structured cooperation between Europol and eu-LISA for information systems and communication infrastructure.
Allocates an estimated EUR 1.053 billion and 910 additional staff posts over the 2028-2034 MFF.
Maintains alignment with the EU data protection framework and fundamental rights standards.

organisation.goals:
The European Policy Centre (EPC) is an independent, not-for-profit think tank dedicated to fostering European integration through analysis and debate, supporting and challenging European decision-makers at all levels to make informed decisions based on evidence and analysis, and providing a platform for engaging partners, stakeholders and citizens in EU policy-making and in the debate about the future of Europe.
In line with its multi-constituency approach, members of the EPC comprise companies, professional and business federations, trade unions, diplomatic missions, regional and local bodies, as well as NGOs representing a broad range of civil society interests, foundations, international and religious organisations. The EPC has around 400 member organisations. Membership changes throughout the year and the latest information can be found on the EPC website which is regularly updated: https://www.epc.eu/en/members

consultation.title: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL establishing a framework of measures for strengthening Europe’s cloud and AI ecosystem (Cloud and AI Development Act)
consultation.summary: The European Commission proposes the Cloud and AI Development Act to establish a framework of measures aimed at strengthening Europe's cloud and artificial intelligence ecosystem. The initiative focuses on three pillars, which include research and innovation for greening infrastructure, industrial investments to triple EU data processing capacity, and actions to increase secure data processing capacities for cloud providers in the EU. Ultimately, the proposal seeks to address infrastructure gaps, reduce critical dependencies on non-European providers, and enhance the Union's digital sovereignty and competitiveness.
key_points: Addresses the EU gap in cloud and AI infrastructure capacity through three distinct pillars.
Promotes research and innovation to accelerate sustainable cloud and AI computing technologies.
Aims to triple the EU data processing capacity over the next 5 to 7 years via industrial investments.
Introduces measures to increase secure data processing capacities for high-critical use cases.
Establishes common criteria for sovereign cloud computing services to reduce extraterritorial dependencies.
Promotes open-source solutions and joint public procurement activities across the public sector.

consultation.title: Public Consultation on the Evaluation of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (Dual-Use Regulation)
consultation.summary: The European Commission has launched a public consultation to evaluate Regulation (EU) 2021/821 on the control of exports, brokering, technical assistance, transit, and transfer of dual-use items. Pursuant to Article 26(4) of the Regulation, the evaluation aims to determine whether the rules have achieved their objectives and remain effective. It also assesses the legislation in light of the evolving global geopolitical landscape and new security threats. Furthermore, the evaluation examines potential ways to reduce administrative burdens for businesses.
key_points: Evaluation of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 on dual-use items
Assessment of whether the Regulation has achieved its objectives
Review of relevance in view of the evolving global geopolitical landscape
Analysis of new threats requiring regulatory adjustments
Identification of ways to reduce administrative burden for businesses

organisation.name: Fédération Générale du Travail de Belgique - Algemeen Belgisch Vakverbond
organisation.goals:
La FGTB est un syndicat qui défend un projet de société. Elle compte aujourd'hui 1.535.000 membres. Elle travaille au jour le jour à plus de justice sociale, à une meilleure répartition des richesses, à plus d’égalité dans le monde du travail.
Elle veille aussi à pouvoir répondre aux préoccupations et inquiétudes de chacun des travailleurs, tout en défendant un projet de société collectif, solidaire et non corporatiste.
Organisation fédérale (ailes wallonne, bruxelloise, flamande), la FGTB (Fédération Générale du Travail de Belgique) veut maintenir une sécurité sociale, une concertation sociale et un droit du travail forts, au niveau fédéral.
La FGTB défend un monde du travail qui place au centre les préoccupations sociales et l’intérêt du travailleur.

consultation.title: Proposal for a COUNCIL DIRECTIVE amending Directives 2003/49/EC, 2009/133/EC, 2011/96/EU, (EU) 2016/1164, (EU)2017/1852, (EU) 2025/50 as regards the simplification of the Union framework on direct taxation and supporting growth and competitiveness of the EU
consultation.summary: The proposal introduces a Council Directive, known as the Omnibus on Taxation, which amends six existing directives in the field of direct taxation to simplify the EU corporate tax framework and support business growth and competitiveness. It aims to reduce administrative and compliance burdens for cross-border activities while maintaining high standards of protection against tax avoidance and abusive practices. The initiative aligns existing rules with international tax developments, such as the Pillar Two global minimum tax, and addresses procedural and legal obstacles in areas like withholding taxes and corporate reorganisations. Overall, the measures seek to improve legal certainty and ensure the coherent functioning of the internal market without lowering tax standards.
key_points: Simplifies the Union framework on direct taxation to reduce compliance costs for businesses.
Eliminates overlapping provisions and addresses practical issues arising from the interaction with the Pillar Two Directive.
Removes procedural barriers and legal uncertainty linked to withholding tax relief.
Maintains existing safeguards and high levels of protection against tax avoidance and evasion.

organisation.name: Institute for European Environmental Policy
organisation.goals: The Institute for European Environmental Policy is a sustainability think tank dedicated to advancing an environmentally sustainable Europe through the analysis and development of policy, and dissemination of research results. Our aim is to contribute to a growing depth of knowledge about Europe and the environment and to analyse and present policy options. We undertake research on the development, implementation and evaluation of environmental and environment-related policies in Europe and the world beyond it. Our focus on European policy making is shared by few and we have a reputation based on being first in the field and possessing a history of knowledge and involvement acquired over nearly forty years.

consultation.title: REPORT FROM THE COMMISSION TO THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT, THE COUNCIL, THE EUROPEAN ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COMMITTEE AND THE COMMITTEE OF THE REGIONS identifying Member States at risk of not meeting the 2030 targets for the reduction of packaging waste and food waste, the preparing for re-use and recycling target for municipal waste, the recycling target for packaging waste and the 2035 municipal waste landfilling reduction target
consultation.summary: The European Commission is preparing the 2027 early warning report to assess Member States progress towards 2030 targets for municipal waste recycling, packaging waste reduction and recycling, and food waste reduction, alongside the 2035 municipal waste landfilling reduction target. The report identifies countries at risk of missing these targets and provides tailored recommendations and best practices to improve their performance. This initiative fulfils a legal obligation under EU waste directives without introducing new policy objectives or requiring an impact assessment. It focuses on evaluating national policies and implementation measures that directly impact waste prevention, separate collection, sorting, and recycling.
key_points: Assess progress towards 2030 waste reduction and recycling targets and 2035 landfill reduction targets.
Identify Member States at risk of not meeting the established targets.
Provide general and country-specific recommendations alongside best practice sharing.
Fulfill legal reporting obligations under the Waste Framework Directive, Packaging and Packaging Waste Directive, and Landfill Directive.
Incorporate data and methodology developed by the European Environment Agency and its European Topic Centre.
Include dedicated country-specific annexes for Member States identified at risk.

consultation.title: Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council and the European Economic and Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions on the creation of a new Atlantic Maritime and Macro-regional Strategy
consultation.summary: The European Commission is preparing a new EU Atlantic Maritime and Macro-regional Strategy to be adopted by June 2027, following a request from the European Council. Building on the existing Atlantic Maritime Strategy and Action Plan, the initiative aims to provide a broader, integrated territorial framework to address shared challenges and opportunities across the Atlantic region. It seeks to improve policy coordination, foster innovative solutions, strengthen multi-level governance, and increase the political weight of Atlantic priorities. The strategy targets the four EU Atlantic Member States and will be established through a non-legislative Communication without an impact assessment.
key_points: Development of a new EU Atlantic Maritime and Macro-regional Strategy by June 2027.
Builds on and integrates the Atlantic Maritime Strategy and the Atlantic Action Plan.
Aims to improve policy coordination across EU, national, and regional levels and funding instruments.
Restricted in scope to the four EU Atlantic Member States: France, Ireland, Portugal, and Spain.
Will incorporate a monitoring framework integrated into the Commission's biennial reports on macro-regional strategies.
Takes the form of a non-legislative Communication from the Commission without requiring an impact assessment.

organisation.name: Rud Pedersen Brussels
organisation.goals: Rud Pedersen Public Affairs is part of Rud Pedersen Group, a leading European public affairs and communications consultancy with owned offices in Brussels, Berlin, Copenhagen, Gothenburg, Helsinki, Kyiv, London, Oslo, Paris, Prague, Roma, Riga, Sofia, Stockholm, Tallinn, The Hague, Vilnius, Madrid, Warsaw and with partner agencies in other European capitals. In Brussels we support our clients in understanding and engaging with the European institutions and the stakeholders that surround them on issues affecting their organisational goals.

consultation.title: Commission Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing diversification instrument to address critical strategic dependencies that expose the Union to economic security risks
consultation.summary: The European Commission is preparing a diversification package, including a new trade instrument and supporting measures, to address critical strategic dependencies on single supplier countries. The initiative aims to accelerate supply chain resilience and reduce economic security risks in critical sectors where non-EU countries may use dependencies as leverage. It combines trade policy measures based on Article 207 TFEU with single market measures based on Article 114 TFEU to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework. This call for evidence invites public and stakeholder feedback to inform the Commission's impact assessment and future legislative work.
key_points: Targets concentrated critical dependencies on dominant supplier countries for strategic sectors.
Proposes a new trade diversification instrument complemented by regulatory and financial support measures.
Combines trade policy measures under Article 207 TFEU and Single Market measures under Article 114 TFEU.
Seeks to address market gaps such as the lack of appropriate price signals and incentives for business de-risking.
Aims to protect the EU from supply chain disruptions, geopolitical pressure, and market volatility.

organisation.name: SEC NEWGATE EU
organisation.goals: SEC Newgate EU is an award-winning Brussels-based public policy and public relations consultancy. We provide issues management, crisis support, media relations, lobbying, association management and the full range of on-line and physical communications tools. Our hallmark is practical action based on analysis, strategic advice and creativity. SEC Newgate EU belongs to the SEC Newgate Group, a global partnership of entrepreneurial agencies specialising in advocacy, public relations and strategic communications.

organisation.name: Transparency International Liaison Office to the European Union
organisation.category: Non-governmental organisations, platforms and networks and similar
organisation.goals:
Transparency International EU is part of the global anti-corruption movement, Transparency International, which includes over 100 chapters around the world. Since 2008, Transparency International EU has functioned as a regional liaison office for the global movement and as such it works closely with the Transparency International Secretariat in Berlin, Germany.
Transparency International EU leads the movement’s EU advocacy, in close cooperation with national chapters worldwide, but particularly with the 24 national chapters in EU Member States.
Transparency International EU’s mission is to prevent corruption and promote integrity, transparency and accountability in EU institutions, policies and legislation.

consultation.short_title: Revision of EU rules on public procurement
consultation.title: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL on public contracts and concessions, repealing Directives 2014/23/EU, 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU, and amending Regulations (EC) No 1370/2007, (EU) 2023/1542, (EU) 2024/1157, (EU) 2024/1252, (EU) 2024/1735, (EU) 2024/1781, (EU) 2024/2847, (EU) 2024/3110 and (EU) 2025/40, and Directives 2008/98/EC, (EU) 2019/882, (EU) 2022/2381, (EU) 2023/1791 and (EU) 2024/1760 (Public Procurement Act)
consultation.summary: The European Commission proposes a revision of EU public procurement rules through a new regulation that repeals the existing 2014 directives on public procurement, utilities, and concessions. The initiative aims to modernize and simplify rules, reduce administrative burdens, and enable preferences for European products in strategic sectors to secure supply chains and add EU value. It also amends multiple sector-specific regulations and directives containing procurement provisions to improve coherence and transparency. Furthermore, the proposal addresses high administrative burdens and legal uncertainty identified in previous evaluations regarding public buyers and businesses.
key_points: Revises and replaces Directives 2014/23/EU, 2014/24/EU, and 2014/25/EU with a single Public Procurement Act regulation.
Enables preference for European products in strategic sectors to ensure security of supply and EU added value.
Aims to modernize and simplify rules, specifically considering EU start-ups and innovators.
Amends various sector-specific regulations and directives that contain public procurement provisions.
Addresses administrative burdens and legal uncertainty that currently affect public buyers and businesses, including SMEs.

consultation.title: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL on the European Union Agency for Criminal Justice Cooperation (Eurojust) and repealing Regulation (EU) 2018/1727
consultation.summary: The European Commission proposes a new regulation on the European Union Agency for Criminal Justice Cooperation (Eurojust) to repeal and replace Regulation (EU) 2018/1727. This initiative responds to an evaluation showing that while Eurojust is indispensable, its operations need greater efficiency and a wider mandate to tackle modern cross-border crime. The proposal expands Eurojust's competence into emerging areas such as cybercrime, gender-based violence, and violations of EU restrictive measures, while transforming it into a more proactive analytical hub. It also aims to streamline the agency's internal structure and improve cooperation with partners like Europol and the European Public Prosecutor Office.
key_points: Repeals and replaces Regulation (EU) 2018/1727 to establish a renewed legal framework for Eurojust.
Expands Eurojust's mandate to cover emerging crime areas including cybercrime, gender-based violence, and violations of EU restrictive measures.
Transforms Eurojust from a reactive coordination body into a strategic and analytical hub for cross-border judicial cooperation.
Standardises National Members' status and powers to improve governance and operational efficiency.
Addresses findings from the 2025 evaluation regarding complex decision-making, wide case scope, and slow procedures with third countries.
Aligns with related revisions of the Europol Regulation, the European Investigation Order Directive, and the European Union Data Protection Regulation.

organisation.name: VERBOND VAN BELGISCHE ONDERNEMINGEN / FEDERATION DES ENTREPRISES DE BELGIQUE
organisation.goals:
Het VBO is de enige interprofessionele werkgeversorganisatie die ondernemingen uit de drie gewesten van ons land vertegenwoordigt. De leden zijn actief in de belangrijkste industrie- en dienstensectoren.
Het VBO heeft de ambitie om:
1. te werken aan een optimaal ondernemingsklimaat;
2. de belangen van bedrijven te verdedigen op federaal, Europees en internationaal niveau;
3. te zorgen voor samenhang in de boodschap en acties van ondernemers.
Daarnaast wil het VBO mee vormgeven aan de beroepen van de toekomst, vooral in de diensten-, industrie- en bouwsector. Het houdt de vinger aan de pols van wat er buiten de organisatie leeft en organiseert tal van ontmoetingen en infosessies met een federale, Europese (zoals de European Business Summit) of internationale dimensie.
De werking van het VBO bestrijkt alle domeinen die verband houden met bedrijfsactiviteiten. Concreet is het actief op economisch, sociaal, juridisch vlak.

organisation.name: WWF European Policy Programme
organisation.category: Non-governmental organisations, platforms and networks and similar
organisation.goals: WWF is an independent conservation organisation, with more than 30 million followers and a global network active through local leadership in over 100 countries. Our mission is to stop the degradation of the planet’s natural environment and to build a future in which people live in harmony with nature, by conserving the world’s biological diversity, ensuring that the use of renewable natural resources is sustainable, and promoting the reduction of pollution and wasteful consumption. The European Policy Office (WWF EU) contributes to the achievement of WWF’s global mission by leading the WWF network to shape EU policies impacting on the European and global environment.

consultation.short_title: EU emissions trading system for maritime, aviation and stationary installations, and market stability reserve - review
consultation.title: Proposal for a DIRECTIVE OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL amending Directive 2003/87/EC and Decision (EU) 2015/1814 as regards driving competitiveness and cost-effective decarbonisation
consultation.summary: The European Commission has published an impact assessment and legislative review concerning Directive 2003/87/EC and Decision (EU) 2015/1814 on the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) and the Market Stability Reserve. This initiative serves as the first part of a broad post-2030 framework package aimed at driving competitiveness and cost-effective decarbonisation. It evaluates how stationary installations, aviation, and maritime sectors can deliver necessary emission reductions while ensuring carbon leakage protection and orderly market functioning. The review addresses the shrinking supply of allowances and adapts the system to align with intermediate 2040 targets and 2050 climate neutrality goals.
key_points: Reviews the EU ETS and the Market Stability Reserve to prepare for post-2030 climate targets.
Assesses pathways toward the 2050 climate neutrality goal and the intermediate 2040 target.
Focuses on industrial sectors, maritime transport, and aviation to ensure cost-effective decarbonisation.
Examines carbon leakage protection, free allocation benchmarks, and the funding transition through EU revenues.
Analyzes market functioning and allowance supply adjustments to prevent trading frictions and price volatility.
Accompanies related proposals simplifying monitoring, reporting, and verification regulations.

organisation.name: industriAll European Trade Union
organisation.goals: Created in 2012 through a merger of 3 European trade union federations, IndustriAll European Trade Union is a federation of independent and democratic trade unions representing manual and non-manual workers in the metal, chemical, energy, mining, textile, clothing and footwear sectors and related industries and activities. We speak for 7 million working men and women united within 200 national trade union affiliates in 39 European countries. Furthermore, we are a member of the European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) and partner of IndustriALL Global Union. We act together, with the aim to combine and optimise strength and complementarities in order to better protect and advance the rights of the workers in our industries and sectors. To achieve this, we follow EU policies related to our members and industries closely.

consultation.short_title: European partnerships implemented as joint undertakings under Horizon Europe (2028-2034)
consultation.title: Single Basic Act for Joint Undertakings and thematic priorities for the European Partnership portfolio in Horizon Europe 28-34
consultation.summary: The European Commission is consulting on the role of European partnerships implemented as joint undertakings under the Horizon Europe framework programme for 2028-2034. The initiative proposes simplifying the instrument by streamlining implementation modes and applying a portfolio approach to identify a limited set of coherent partnerships. These partnerships will feature objectives closely aligned with the Competitiveness Fund. Furthermore, the proposal suggests establishing joint undertakings under Article 187 TFEU through a single basic act with harmonised rules.
key_points: Streamline implementation modes for European partnerships under Horizon Europe 2028-2034
Use a portfolio approach to identify a limited set of coherent partnerships
Align partnership objectives closely with the Competitiveness Fund
Establish joint undertakings under Article 187 TFEU with clear added value
Implement a single basic act with harmonised rules for joint undertakings

organisation.name: logos public affairs
organisation.goals:
logos is an integrated advocacy consultancy within the mci group, an independent global marketing communications group.
We provide tailor-made public affairs, association management, communication solutions and high-level industry/policy dialogues.
Technological advancements, climate change, and globalization are driving industries to converge and transform the way we live, work, move, and consume. We guide clients in making positive changes by providing compelling evidence for innovation-friendly public policy.
Our specialisation lies in three main sectorial clusters: sustainability, energy and mobility, aerospace and defence, technology and telecommunications, and strategic alliances resulting from industry convergence.
logos acquired Business Bridge (BBE) in 2022, a boutique agency known for its C-level political conferences: the European Space Conference, the Energy and lndustry Conference (previously EnerGreenDeal Conference), and the European Defence & Security Conference.
